thought_title: Three mysteries worked in God's silence

edition.witness_note: Lake 1912 Loeb copy-text; Lightfoot/Funk middle recension not yet locked as second witness

source_text: [1] Καὶ ἔλαθεν τὸν ἄρχοντα τοῦ αἰῶνος τούτου ἡ παρθενία Μαρίας καὶ ὁ τοκετὸς αὐτῆς, ὁμοίως καὶ ὁ θάνατος τοῦ κυρίου: τρία μυστήρια κραυγῆς, ἅτινα ἐν ἡσυχίᾳ θεοῦ ἐπράχθη. [2] πῶς οὖν ἐφανερώθη τοῖς αἰῶσιν; ἀστὴρ ἐν οὐρανῷ ἔλαμψεν ὑπὲρ πάντας τοὺς ἀστέρας, καὶ τὸ φῶς αὐτοῦ ἀνεκλάλητον ἦν καὶ ξενισμὸν παρεῖχεν ἡ καινότης αὐτοῦ, τὰ δὲ λοιπὰ πάντα ἄστρα ἅμα ἡλίῳ καὶ σελήνῃ χορὸς ἐγένετο τῷ ἀστέρι, αὐτὸς δὲ ἦν ὑπερβάλλων τὸ φῶς αὐτοῦ ὑπὲρ πάντα: ταραχή τε ἦν, πόθεν ἡ καινότης ἡ ἀνόμοιος αὐτοῖς. [3] ὅθεν ἐλύετο πᾶσα μαγεία καὶ πᾶς δεσμὸς ἠφανίζετο κακίας: ἄγνοια καθῃρεῖτο, παλαιὰ βασιλεία διεφθείρετο θεοῦ ἀνθρωπίνως φανερουμένου εἰς καινότητα ἀϊδίου ζωῆς: ἀρχὴν δὲ ἐλάμβανεν τὸ παρὰ θεῷ ἀπηρτισμένον. ἔνθεν τὰ πάντα συνεκινεῖτο διὰ τὸ μελετᾶσθαι θανάτου κατάλυσιν.
pass_a_gloss: And the virginity of Mary and her giving birth escaped the notice of the ruler of this age, as did also the death of the Lord: three mysteries of a loud cry, which were accomplished in the silence of God. How then was he revealed to the ages? A star shone in heaven beyond all the stars, and its light was beyond telling, and its newness caused amazement. All the rest of the stars, together with sun and moon, became a chorus to the star, but it was surpassing them all with its light. And there was confusion about where this newness, unlike them, came from. From then on all magic was being dissolved and every bond of wickedness was vanishing; ignorance was being torn down, the old kingdom was being destroyed, as God was being revealed in human fashion for the newness of eternal life. What had been made complete with God was taking its beginning. From then on all things were stirred together, because the destruction of death was being worked out.

lemmas.gloss: stir up together, set in motion
be practiced, be planned, be carried out

pass_b_english: The ruler of this age never noticed Mary's virginity or her giving birth, nor the death of the Lord (1 Corinthians 2:6-8). These are three mysteries meant to be shouted aloud, yet God worked them in silence.

How, then, was he revealed to the ages? A star blazed in heaven, brighter than all the stars (Matthew 2:2, 9). Its light was beyond words, and its newness was astonishing. All the other stars, with the sun and the moon, gathered as a chorus around that star, but its light outshone them all. And there was confusion: where had this new thing come from, so unlike them?

From that moment all magic began to come undone, and every chain of wickedness disappeared. Ignorance was torn down. The old kingdom fell to ruin, for God was appearing in human form to bring the newness of eternal life. What had been made ready with God now began. And so all things were shaken together, because the destruction of death was under way.

choices.term: τρία μυστήρια κραυγῆς, ἅτινα ἐν ἡσυχίᾳ θεοῦ ἐπράχθη
choices.english: three mysteries meant to be shouted aloud, yet God worked them in silence
choices.why: Ignatius's paradox: mysteries of a cry, done in God's stillness. κραυγή is a shout, so they are made for proclamation.
rejected: mysteries of renown (ANF; loses the shout/silence contrast)

choices.why: τοκετός is the act of childbirth, not the child.

choices.english: because the destruction of death was under way
choices.why: Passive infinitive with no stated subject: the abolition of death was being carried out.
rejected: because He meditated the abolition of death (ANF; supplies a subject and narrows μελετάω to thinking)

choices.english: God was appearing in human form
choices.why: Genitive absolute; ἀνθρωπίνως means in a human way.
rejected: God Himself being manifested in human form (ANF; close)

anf_compare.notes: Mostly aligned. ANF 'her offspring' should be her giving birth (τοκετός); 'mysteries of renown' blunts κραυγῆς (a cry); 'He meditated the abolition of death' supplies a subject the passive infinitive μελετᾶσθαι does not have. 'so unlike to everything else [in the heavens]' adds a bracketed gloss.

bible_refs.note: ἀρχόντων τοῦ αἰῶνος τούτου: the rulers of this age did not know God's hidden wisdom

notes: Whole chapter 19 (sections 1-3) matches the ANF span.
Possible echoes kept out of the reading text: Romans 6:4 (newness of life, καινότητι ζωῆς); 2 Timothy 1:10 and 1 Corinthians 15:26 (death abolished); Genesis 37:9 (sun, moon, and stars bowing).

review.notes: Paragraph [1] clauses [1]–[3] checked against Pass A and Pass B. Source is Ignatius, Ephesians 19 (virginity, childbirth, the Lord’s death; the star; magic and the old kingdom). Pass A keeps ἔλαθεν as ‘escaped the notice of the ruler of this age’, ‘τρία μυστήρια κραυγῆς, ἅτινα ἐν ἡσυχίᾳ θεοῦ ἐπράχθη’ as ‘three mysteries of a loud cry, which were accomplished in the silence of God’, and ‘τὸ παρὰ θεῷ ἀπηρτισμένον’ as ‘made complete’. Pass B ‘The ruler of this age never noticed’ does not reverse that fact, but ‘meant to be shouted aloud, yet God worked them in silence’ adds purpose and an agent; ‘to bring the newness of eternal life’ adds a verb to ‘εἰς καινότητα ἀϊδίου ζωῆς’; ‘made ready’ contradicts A’s ‘made complete’. Imperfects ‘πᾶς δεσμὸς ἠφανίζετο κακίας’ and ‘παλαιὰ βασιλεία διεφθείρετο’ become completed ‘disappeared’ and ‘fell to ruin’. Inline (1 Corinthians 2:6-8) and (Matthew 2:2, 9) match the supplied bible_refs; the practice is not failed. Title names the three-mysteries thought. No OCR debris in the locked text.
reasons: Agency and modality: Pass B ‘These are three mysteries meant to be shouted aloud, yet God worked them in silence’ adds purpose (‘meant to be’) and makes God the worker, against Greek ‘τρία μυστήρια κραυγῆς, ἅτινα ἐν ἡσυχίᾳ θεοῦ ἐπράχθη’ and Pass A ‘three mysteries of a loud cry, which were accomplished in the silence of God’.

Modality: Pass B ‘for God was appearing in human form to bring the newness of eternal life’ inserts the purpose verb ‘to bring’, against Greek ‘θεοῦ ἀνθρωπίνως φανερουμένου εἰς καινότητα ἀϊδίου ζωῆς’ and Pass A ‘as God was being revealed in human fashion for the newness of eternal life’.

Doctrine: Pass B ‘What had been made ready with God now began’ contradicts Pass A ‘What had been made complete with God was taking its beginning’ and weakens Greek ‘ἀρχὴν δὲ ἐλάμβανεν τὸ παρὰ θεῷ ἀπηρτισμένον’.

Modality: Pass B ‘every chain of wickedness disappeared’ and ‘The old kingdom fell to ruin’ turn the imperfects in ‘πᾶς δεσμὸς ἠφανίζετο κακίας’ and ‘παλαιὰ βασιλεία διεφθείρετο’ into finished events, against Pass A ‘every bond of wickedness was vanishing’ and ‘the old kingdom was being destroyed’.
